# Agent Artifact Protocol (AAP)

> AAP makes repository context addressable without requiring it to be loaded. It is a small filesystem convention: one checked-in map file (`.aap/map.yaml`) that tells an agent where things live and which neighboring repositories exist, validated by a JSON Schema. It is not a context engine, RAG, agent framework, dependency graph or authorization system.

Version: 0.3.0 (experimental, pre-1.0). Pin the tag `v0.3.0`; do not read the default branch tip as authoritative.

## If you are an agent working in a repository

1. Look for the map in this order: `.aap/map.yaml`, `map.yaml`, `docs/map.yaml`.
2. Read that one file. That is the whole orientation step (level L0). Do not open anything else yet.
3. Pick one `layout` key (`code`, `tests`, `artifacts`, `scratch`, ...) or one `nodes` entry for the task, and open only that path (L1).
4. Open a single durable artifact only if the task needs durable memory (L2). Use normal code tools for the rest (L3).
5. A node with a `map` pointer is a hop you may take on purpose. Never open linked maps recursively "to be safe".
6. Do not fetch this upstream repository or read SPEC.md at session start. The local map is the source of truth for the checkout.

If there is no map and the user wants one, use the `aap-map` skill (see below) or copy `templates/minimal-map.yaml` to `.aap/map.yaml` and edit it. Never overwrite an existing map without explicit confirmation.

## The map in one screen

```yaml
version: 2
workspace: { id: my-app, description: What this checkout is }
self: { id: my-app, kind: repository, path: . }
layout:
  code: src/
  tests: tests/
  artifacts: docs/artifacts/
  scratch: docs/scratch/
nodes: []
```

- `id` values are lowercase kebab-case and start with a letter.
- `layout` maps intent to a path in this checkout. Paths are relative, never absolute, never contain `..`. Paths may be absent on disk; do not invent a directory tree to satisfy the map.
- `nodes` are direct navigation hops to other repositories or products. They are not a dependency graph. Keep them few.
- Machine-local checkout paths go in a gitignored `map.local.yaml` (`overlays`), not in the committed map.

## The `access` rules (write fence)

Every layout value is either a path string or `{ path, access?, description? }`.

- A string means `{ path: <string>, access: read-write }`. A missing `access` means `read-write`.
- `access` is `read-only` or `read-write`. Nothing else.
- `read-only`: you may read it, you must not create or change durable content there.
- When a layout key lists several paths, the durable write home is the first entry whose access is not `read-only`.
- If a key has no writable entry, stop and ask. Do not invent a parallel root and do not write into a read-only one.
- On a node, `access: read-only` means do not modify that repository from this workspace (typical for external products).
- A node's `write: [...]` list is a role hint, not a permission. It never overrides `access`.
- `overlays` only say where a node is checked out on this machine. They never grant write rights.
- All of this is a coordination fence between agents and humans. Real enforcement is Git permissions, CODEOWNERS, protected branches and sandboxes.

Until the user or runtime explicitly enables writes, prefer reading and orienting only.

## Where to read next (only when needed)

- Normative spec, short: https://github.com/gitpash/agent-artifact-protocol/blob/v0.3.0/SPEC.md
- Map JSON Schema (draft-07): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitpash/agent-artifact-protocol/v0.3.0/schemas/map.schema.json
- Starter map: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitpash/agent-artifact-protocol/v0.3.0/templates/minimal-map.yaml
- Examples (single repo, multi-repo hub, resource refs): `examples/` in the same tag
- Optional profiles (stream packs, done bar, hub umbrella, CI validation): `cookbook/README.md`. These are never part of the mandatory first read.
- Validator for this repo: `pip install pyyaml jsonschema && python scripts/validate.py`

## Creating or updating a map: the `aap-map` skill

The folder `skills/aap-map/` is a portable agent skill (one SKILL.md). It looks at a codebase, writes a minimal map, and flags guesses for human review. It does not need any tools installed. Install commands are at the top of the README.

## Rules of thumb

- Keep the map sparse. If a map did not help on a real task, shrink it before adding anything.
- Prefer omitting a layout key over pointing it at a path that does not exist.
- A node needs one concrete reason to exist: you would plausibly open that repository during a normal change here. A mention in a README is not enough.
- Schema-valid does not mean useful. A human should review nodes before the map is relied on.
